questions: If Takahashi moves from one building to another via a walkway, does the floor number X have to be exactly the same in both buildings, or can he choose any floor ≤ X that exists in the adjacent building?
When using a walkway, is it allowed to move to a building that has exactly X floors, or must it have strictly more than X floors?
Are walkways usable in both directions simultaneously, i.e., can Takahashi move from building A to B and later back from B to A without any additional cost?
Does Takahashi have to stay within the grid boundaries, or can he move outside the city (e.g., from a border building to a non‑existent adjacent block) and what happens then?
If multiple walkways are possible at the same floor, does Takahashi have to choose one, or can he split his path arbitrarily (e.g., teleport) without using stairs?
Are there any limits on the total number of moves (stairs + walkways) Takahashi can make, or can he loop indefinitely as long as the stair count is minimized?
In the case where the start and target floors are the same (Y_i = Z_i) but the buildings differ, is the answer always zero stairs, or must he still use at least one stair move to change buildings?
Should the answer be printed as a 64‑bit integer, and what should be done if the minimal number of stairs exceeds the range of a 32‑bit signed integer?
answers: Floor level must be exactly the same in both buildings for a walkway to be usable.

inline_prompts:
There is a city divided into H \times W blocks, and there is exactly one building in each block.
Specifically, in the block at the i-th row from the north (1\leq i\leq H) and the j-th column from the west (1\leq j\leq W) (hereafter referred to as block (i,j)), there is a building of F_{i,j} floors.
Takahashi has two ways of moving. If he is on the X-th floor (1\leq X\leq F_{i,j}) of the building in block (i,j), he can:
- Move up or down one floor within the same building using stairs. If X=1, he cannot move down; if X=F_{i,j}, he cannot move up.
- Choose a building with at least X floors in a cardinally adjacent block, and move to the X-th floor of that building using a (sky) walkway. Floor level must be exactly the same in both buildings for a walkway to be usable.
Here, two blocks (i,j) and (i',j') are cardinally adjacent if and only if \lvert i - i'\rvert + \lvert j - j'\rvert = 1.
You are given Q queries to be answered. The i-th query (1\leq i\leq Q) is the following.
Find the minimum possible number of times that Takahashi uses stairs to move from the Y_i-th floor of the building in block (A_i,B_i) to the Z_i-th floor of the building in block (C_i,D_i).
The count of times using stairs is incremented each time he moves up or down one floor, possibly multiple times within the same building. (For example, moving from the 1st floor to the 6th floor of a building counts as 5 uses of stairs.)
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
H W
F_{1,1} F_{1,2} \ldots F_{1,W}
F_{2,1} F_{2,2} \ldots F_{2,W}
\vdots
F_{H,1} F_{H,2} \ldots F_{H,W}
Q
A_1 B_1 Y_1 C_1 D_1 Z_1
A_2 B_2 Y_2 C_2 D_2 Z_2
\vdots
A_Q B_Q Y_Q C_Q D_Q Z_Q
Output
Print Q lines. The i-th line should contain the answer to the i-th query as an integer.
Constraints
- 1\leq H \leq 500
- 1\leq W \leq 500
- 1\leq F_{i,j}
